# seams"). This is a coarse backstop that complements the precise ESLint rules
# in eslint.config.mjs — it catches a violation even if lint is skipped, and
# documents the invariants in one readable place.
#

fail=0
SRC="src"

report() {
  # $1 = human description, $2 = matching lines (empty = ok)
  if [[ -n "$2" ]]; then
    printf '\033[31m✗ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"
    printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed 's/^/    /'
    fail=1
  else
    printf '\033[32m✓ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"
  fi
}

# 1. ipcRenderer only in the preload bridge.
hits=$(grep -rnw 'ipcRenderer' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/preload/' || ******)
report "ipcRenderer used only in src/preload/" "$hits"

# 2. Host primitives (fs / child_process / chokidar / node-pty) only in LocalHost.
hits=$(grep -rnE "from ['\"](node:)?(fs|fs/promises|child_process)['\"]|from ['\"](chokidar|node-pty)['\"]|import\(['\"]((node:)?(fs|fs/promises|child_process)|chokidar|node-pty)['\"]\)" \
  "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/project-host/local-host.ts' || ******)
report "host primitives imported only in local-host.ts" "$hits"

# 3. PTY spawning (host.spawnPty call sites) only in the supervisor.
hits=$(grep -rnE '\.spawnPty\(' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/pty/pty-supervisor.ts' || ******)
report "host.spawnPty() called only in pty-supervisor.ts" "$hits"

# 4. Bundled harness identities stay inside provider-owned main modules. Shared
# IPC, persistence, and renderer code treat provider ids as opaque catalog data.
hits=$(grep -rnE "['\"](plain-shell|claude-code|codex)['\"]" \
  "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/harness/' || ******)
report "bundled harness ids used only in src/main/harness/" "$hits"

# 5. Raw loopback streams are transport for the main-owned pane proxy, never a
# renderer, IPC, harness, or feature-level socket API.
hits=$(grep -rnE '\.connectLoopback\(' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/web-pane/loopback-http-proxy.ts' || ******)
report "host.connectLoopback() called only in the web-pane proxy" "$hits"

# 6. ipcMain is a single transport choke point. Feature registrars receive the
# narrow IpcRegistrar capability and cannot install handlers directly.
hits=$(grep -rnw 'ipcMain' "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -v '^src/main/ipc/authority-router.ts' || ******)
report "ipcMain used only in the IPC authority router" "$hits"

# 7. Feature registrars cannot bypass central renderer-owner or canonical-path
# authority resolution.
hits=$(grep -rnE '\.currentOwner\(|\.realpath\(|getRegisteredWorkspaceRoot|\basHostId\b|\bdirnameHostPath\b' \
  'src/main/ipc/features' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' || ******)
report "IPC features use central owner/path authority" "$hits"

# 8. ssh2 is an implementation detail of the remote ProjectHost adapter. Main
# consumers continue to depend on ProjectHost and host-qualified paths only.
hits=$(grep -rnE "from ['\"]ssh2['\"]|import\(['\"]ssh2['\"]\)" \
  "$SRC" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -vE '^src/main/project-host/ssh-(client-lifecycle|host|host-options|file-access|exclusive-create|project-file-transfer|abort|transport-pool|watch-service)\.ts' || ******)
report "ssh2 details stay inside the SshHost adapter" "$hits"

# 9. Host-local collaborators share SshHost's authentication lifecycle. They
# receive authenticated clients through narrow ports and never construct one.

  src/main/project-host/ssh-{client-lifecycle,file-access,exclusive-create,project-file-transfer,transport-pool,watch-service}.ts || ******)
report "SSH collaborators do not create independent clients" "$hits"

hits=$(grep -nE 'Ssh(FileAccess|TransportPool|WatchService|AuthenticationLifecycle)|startSshAuthentication' \
  src/main/project-host/index.ts || ******)
report "only SshHost is exported as the remote host façade" "$hits"

# construct SSH hosts. Project persistence/workflows cannot import concrete host
# owners, and the catalog cannot depend on project persistence/workflows.

  grep -rnE '\bnew SshHost\(' src/main --include='*.ts' --include='*.mts' \
    | grep -v '^src/main/project-host/project-host-catalog.ts' || ******
  grep -nE "RendererSshPrompter|SshHostTrustStore|LocalSshIdentitySource|parseSshConfig|known-hosts|identityFileCandidates|from ['\"]\./project-host/(ssh-host|ssh-host-trust|ssh-identity-source|renderer-ssh-prompter|project-host-catalog)['\"]" \
    src/main/project-registry.ts src/main/project-coordinator.ts || ******
  grep -nE "from ['\"][^'\"]*(project-registry|project-coordinator)['\"]" \
    src/main/project-host/project-host-catalog.ts src/main/project-host/project-host.ts || ******
  sed -n '/^export class ProjectRegistry/,$p' src/main/project-registry.ts \
    | grep -nE '^  (public )?(async )?(listHosts|hostById|connectedHosts|connectHost|disconnectHost|disconnectSshHosts|browseHost)[(:=]' || ******
})
report "SSH construction and implementation owners stay in the host catalog" "$hits"

# capability constructs a git invocation against the host directly.
hits=$(grep -rnF ".exec('git'" src/main/git --include='*.ts' --include='*.mts' \
  | grep -vE '^src/main/git/(git-command-context|worker-host-broker)\.ts' || ******)
report "Git commands use the shared command context" "$hits"

# 13. The utility-process proxy implements only Git's exact exec/read/metadata port,
# rather than pretending to be a complete ProjectHost with never placeholders.
hits=$(grep -nE 'implements ProjectHost|execStream\(\): never|spawnPty\(\): never|connectLoopback\(\): never|readFile\(\): never|writeFile\(\): never|readdir\(\): never|stat\(\): never|realpath\(\): never|watch\(\): never' \
  src/workers/git-worker.ts || ******)
report "Git worker proxy exposes only exact exec, read, and metadata operations" "$hits"

if [[ "$fail" -ne 0 ]]; then
  printf '\n\033[31mseam check failed\033[0m\n'
  exit 1
fi
printf '\nseam check passed\n'

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
      - 'epic/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ******

jobs:
  release-version-integrity:
    name: Release version integrity
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      github.actor == 'github-actions[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'github-actions[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'release/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out trusted release validation
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |-
            scripts/validate-release-pr.mts
            scripts/release-github-evidence.mts
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Validate version-only release change
        env:
          GITHUB_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_PR_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          RELEASE_PR_MODE: pre-merge
          RELEASE_PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: node scripts/validate-release-pr.mts

  verify:
    name: Verification (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      issues: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Architecture validates the exact event base/head and accepted epic history.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run policy, type, and test verification
        env:
          HVIR_REPO_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: npm run verify

  electron-smoke:
    name: Electron smoke (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run production Electron workflow
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/production
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke

      - name: Run development renderer Performance Timeline containment
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/development-performance
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke:development-performance

      - name: Prove failure and interruption isolation
        run: xvfb-run -a npm run smoke:isolation

{"file_text":"# hvir

> **A lightweight, view-first workbench for agentic development.**

`hvir` is a desktop workbench purpose-built for working alongside AI coding agents and CLI harnesses (such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and custom agent workflows). It pairs high-performance terminal multiplexing with rich visual document inspection, interactive Git graphs, side-by-side diff review, embedded web previews, and first-class remote development over SSH.

---

## ✨ Features

### 🤖 Agent Harness Integration
- **Bundled Providers**: Native integration with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Pi, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, plain shells, and custom CLI commands.
- **Harness Profiles & Telemetry**: Configurable provider profiles, usage demand controllers, session discovery, context telemetry hubs, and token usage tracking.
- **Image & File Staging**: Remote and local clipboard image/file pasting for multimodal agent interaction.
- **Composer Modes**: Configurable submission behaviors tailored for agent workflows.

### 💻 Modern Terminal Experience
- **Ghostty Web + Native PTY**: Fast terminal rendering powered by WebAssembly Ghostty (`ghostty-web`) backed by supervised native pseudo-terminals (`node-pty`).
- **Flexible Layouts**: Split panes, horizon views, active terminal focus preservation, and workspace reordering.
- **Terminal Polish**: Semantic navigation, font ligature support, customizable color themes with a built-in catalog, search, and middle-click closing.

### 📄 View-First Document Editor & Renderers
- **CodeMirror 6 Editor**: Fast text editing with syntax highlighting powered by Shiki.
- **Rich Document Rendering**:
  - Markdown preview with GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) task lists and KaTeX mathematical notation.
  - Interactive Mermaid diagram rendering.
  - Structured data viewing for CSV and JSON files.
  - Sandboxed HTML preview.
- **Workspace Navigation**: Primary/secondary pane splitting, tab pinning, file tree management, and live file-change reloading.

### 🔀 Document Review & Git Workspace
- **Document Review Workspace**: Dedicated diff review mode with side-by-side or unified inline diffs, diff-base switching, and direct review delivery into agent terminal sessions.
- **Visual Git Panel & Graph**: Interactive branch switching, worktree management, commit history visualization, dirty-file tracking, and stage/unstage controls.
- **Isolated Git Workers**: Heavy repository analysis and Git operations run inside dedicated background utility processes.

### 🌐 Local & Remote (SSH) Workspaces
- **Projects Bar**: Seamlessly switch between multiple local projects and remote workspaces.
- **Full-Featured SSH Remotes**: Built-in SSH client connection pool (`ssh2`), automated `~/.ssh/config` parsing, host key verification, remote file watching, and secure file transfers.

### 🌐 In-App Web Previews (Web Pane)
- **Embedded Browser Pane**: Preview local development servers, web applications, and documentation directly within the workbench.
- **Loopback Proxy**: Built-in loopback HTTP proxy and route registry for isolated, secure web previews.

### 🩺 Observability, Diagnostics & Self-Healing
- **Workbench Health Monitoring**: Real-time diagnostic logging and journal collection.
- **Renderer Recovery**: Automatic detection and graceful recovery from renderer process interruptions.
- **Cross-Session Projections**: Aggregate metrics and history across working sessions.

---

## 🏗 Architecture

`hvir` is built on Electron, React 19, TypeScript, and Vite, adhering to strict security and architectural seams:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Renderer Process                    │
│   React 19 • CodeMirror 6 • Ghostty Web • Git Graph UI  │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                             │ ContextBridge IPC (Safe Channels)
┌────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│                    Preload & IPC Layer                  │
│       Authority Router • IPC Contract Capabilities       │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                             │
┌────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│                       Main Process                      │
│  ┌───────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ LocalHost/SshHost │  │ PTY Supervisor & Registry  │  │
│  ├───────────────────┤  ├────────────────────────────┤  │
│  │ Harness Registry  │  │ Diagnostics & Health Hub   │  │
│  └───────────────────┘  └────────────────────────────┘  │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                             │ Utility Process IPC
┌────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│                     Worker Processes                    │
│            Git Worker • Native Host Utilities           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **`src/main`**: Central host coordinator managing local and SSH environments, PTY lifecycles, harness providers, file operations, and IPC authority policies.
- **`src/preload`**: Context-isolated bridge exposing strictly typed, capability-bounded APIs to the renderer.
- **`src/renderer`**: UI layer composed of the workspace shell, split views, terminal canvases, file trees, and settings dialogs.
- **`src/workers`**: Standalone Node utility processes that offload compute-heavy tasks like Git operations without blocking the main event loop.
- **`src/shared`**: Shared TypeScript types, IPC contracts, and utility protocols.
- **`packages/rename-noreplace`**: Native Node addon providing atomic rename operations.

---

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- **Node.js**: `v24.0.0` or later
- **npm**: `v10.0.0` or later
- **C/C++ Build Toolchain**: Required for compiling native modules (`node-gyp`, `node-pty`, `@hvir/rename-noreplace`)
  - **macOS**: Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`)
  - **Linux**: `build-essential`, `python3`, and standard C++ libraries

### Installation

1. Clone the repository:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/jarmak-personal/hvir.git
   cd hvir
   ```

2. Install dependencies (this will automatically compile native modules and configure runtime dependencies):
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

### Running in Development

Start the development environment with hot reloading:

```bash
npm run dev
```

---

## 🛠 Available Scripts

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Starts the Electron and Vite development server with hot-reload |
| `npm run build` | Runs typechecks and compiles production assets with `electron-vite` |
| `npm test` | Executes the unit and integration test suite using Vitest |
| `npm run test:watch` | Runs Vitest in interactive watch mode |
| `npm run typecheck` | Runs TypeScript compiler checks across Node and Web targets |
| `npm run lint` | Lints the codebase with ESLint |
| `npm run format:check` | Verifies formatting rules with Prettier |
| `npm run format` | Auto-formats code with Prettier |
| `npm run check-seams` | Verifies architectural boundaries and module import rules |
| `npm run architecture:report` | Analyzes module dependencies and architectural hotspots |
| `npm run smoke` | Runs the automated Electron smoke test scenario suite |
| `npm run pack:mac:arm64` | Packages a macOS Apple Silicon distributable (`.pkg`) |
| `npm run pack:linux:x64` | Packages a Linux x64 distributable (`.deb`) |
| `npm run pack:linux:arm64` | Packages a Linux ARM64 distributable (`.deb`) |

---

## 🔒 Security & Architecture Guardrails

`hvir` enforces strict modularity and security boundaries:

- **Isolated Host Primitives**: Direct file-system and process spawning primitives are constrained to host adapters (`LocalHost` and `SshHost`).
- **Preload Isolation**: Renderer code cannot access raw Node.js or Electron internals; all communication passes through typed IPC interfaces.
- **Strict Seam Enforcement**: Run `npm run check-seams` to validate that module separation rules are maintained.

---

## 📄 License

This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

# hvir

> **A lightweight, view-first workbench for agentic development.**

`hvir` is a desktop workbench purpose-built for working alongside AI coding agents and CLI harnesses (such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and custom agent workflows). It pairs high-performance terminal multiplexing with rich visual document inspection, interactive Git graphs, side-by-side diff review, embedded web previews, and first-class remote development over SSH.

---

## ✨ Features

### 🤖 Agent Harness Integration
- **Bundled Providers**: Native integration with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Pi, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, plain shells, and custom CLI commands.
- **Harness Profiles & Telemetry**: Configurable provider profiles, usage demand controllers, session discovery, context telemetry hubs, and token usage tracking.
- **Image & File Staging**: Remote and local clipboard image/file pasting for multimodal agent interaction.
- **Composer Modes**: Configurable submission behaviors tailored for agent workflows.

### 💻 Modern Terminal Experience
- **Ghostty Web + Native PTY**: Fast terminal rendering powered by WebAssembly Ghostty (`ghostty-web`) backed by supervised native pseudo-terminals (`node-pty`).
- **Flexible Layouts**: Split panes, horizon views, active terminal focus preservation, and workspace reordering.
- **Terminal Polish**: Semantic navigation, font ligature support, customizable color themes with a built-in catalog, search, and middle-click closing.

### 📄 View-First Document Editor & Renderers
- **CodeMirror 6 Editor**: Fast text editing with syntax highlighting powered by Shiki.
- **Rich Document Rendering**:
  - Markdown preview with GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) task lists and KaTeX mathematical notation.
  - Interactive Mermaid diagram rendering.
  - Structured data viewing for CSV and JSON files.
  - Sandboxed HTML preview.
- **Workspace Navigation**: Primary/secondary pane splitting, tab pinning, file tree management, and live file-change reloading.

### 🔀 Document Review & Git Workspace
- **Document Review Workspace**: Dedicated diff review mode with side-by-side or unified inline diffs, diff-base switching, and direct review delivery into agent terminal sessions.
- **Visual Git Panel & Graph**: Interactive branch switching, worktree management, commit history visualization, dirty-file tracking, and stage/unstage controls.
- **Isolated Git Workers**: Heavy repository analysis and Git operations run inside dedicated background utility processes.

### 🌐 Local & Remote (SSH) Workspaces
- **Projects Bar**: Seamlessly switch between multiple local projects and remote workspaces.
- **Full-Featured SSH Remotes**: Built-in SSH client connection pool (`ssh2`), automated `~/.ssh/config` parsing, host key verification, remote file watching, and secure file transfers.

### 🌐 In-App Web Previews (Web Pane)
- **Embedded Browser Pane**: Preview local development servers, web applications, and documentation directly within the workbench.
- **Loopback Proxy**: Built-in loopback HTTP proxy and route registry for isolated, secure web previews.

### 🩺 Observability, Diagnostics & Self-Healing
- **Workbench Health Monitoring**: Real-time diagnostic logging and journal collection.
- **Renderer Recovery**: Automatic detection and graceful recovery from renderer process interruptions.
- **Cross-Session Projections**: Aggregate metrics and history across working sessions.

---

## 🏗 Architecture

`hvir` is built on Electron, React 19, TypeScript, and Vite, adhering to strict security and architectural seams:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Renderer Process                    │
│   React 19 • CodeMirror 6 • Ghostty Web • Git Graph UI  │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                             │ ContextBridge IPC (Safe Channels)
┌────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│                    Preload & IPC Layer                  │
│       Authority Router • IPC Contract Capabilities       │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                             │
┌────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│                       Main Process                      │
│  ┌───────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ LocalHost/SshHost │  │ PTY Supervisor & Registry  │  │
│  ├───────────────────┤  ├────────────────────────────┤  │
│  │ Harness Registry  │  │ Diagnostics & Health Hub   │  │
│  └───────────────────┘  └────────────────────────────┘  │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                             │ Utility Process IPC
┌────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│                     Worker Processes                    │
│            Git Worker • Native Host Utilities           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **`src/main`**: Central host coordinator managing local and SSH environments, PTY lifecycles, harness providers, file operations, and IPC authority policies.
- **`src/preload`**: Context-isolated bridge exposing strictly typed, capability-bounded APIs to the renderer.
- **`src/renderer`**: UI layer composed of the workspace shell, split views, terminal canvases, file trees, and settings dialogs.
- **`src/workers`**: Standalone Node utility processes that offload compute-heavy tasks like Git operations without blocking the main event loop.
- **`src/shared`**: Shared TypeScript types, IPC contracts, and utility protocols.
- **`packages/rename-noreplace`**: Native Node addon providing atomic rename operations.

---

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- **Node.js**: `v24.0.0` or later
- **npm**: `v10.0.0` or later
- **C/C++ Build Toolchain**: Required for compiling native modules (`node-gyp`, `node-pty`, `@hvir/rename-noreplace`)
  - **macOS**: Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`)
  - **Linux**: `build-essential`, `python3`, and standard C++ libraries

### Installation

1. Clone the repository:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/jarmak-personal/hvir.git
   cd hvir
   ```

2. Install dependencies (this will automatically compile native modules and configure runtime dependencies):
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

### Running in Development

Start the development environment with hot reloading:

```bash
npm run dev
```

---

## 🛠 Available Scripts

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Starts the Electron and Vite development server with hot-reload |
| `npm run build` | Runs typechecks and compiles production assets with `electron-vite` |
| `npm test` | Executes the unit and integration test suite using Vitest |
| `npm run test:watch` | Runs Vitest in interactive watch mode |
| `npm run typecheck` | Runs TypeScript compiler checks across Node and Web targets |
| `npm run lint` | Lints the codebase with ESLint |
| `npm run format:check` | Verifies formatting rules with Prettier |
| `npm run format` | Auto-formats code with Prettier |
| `npm run check-seams` | Verifies architectural boundaries and module import rules |
| `npm run architecture:report` | Analyzes module dependencies and architectural hotspots |
| `npm run smoke` | Runs the automated Electron smoke test scenario suite |
| `npm run pack:mac:arm64` | Packages a macOS Apple Silicon distributable (`.pkg`) |
| `npm run pack:linux:x64` | Packages a Linux x64 distributable (`.deb`) |
| `npm run pack:linux:arm64` | Packages a Linux ARM64 distributable (`.deb`) |

---

## 🔒 Security & Architecture Guardrails

`hvir` enforces strict modularity and security boundaries:

- **Isolated Host Primitives**: Direct file-system and process spawning primitives are constrained to host adapters (`LocalHost` and `SshHost`).
- **Preload Isolation**: Renderer code cannot access raw Node.js or Electron internals; all communication passes through typed IPC interfaces.
- **Strict Seam Enforcement**: Run `npm run check-seams` to validate that module separation rules are maintained.

---

## 📄 License

This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
